title: Peak lumbar back muscle EMG during symmetric 10 kg lifts from knee/ankle height, near/far, no exoskeleton

quantity.name: peak back muscle EMG
quantity.definition: peak over lift of normalised EMG averaged over left/right iliocostalis and longissimus pars lumborum; mean ± SD over subjects (error bars assumed SD)

source.authors: Koopman AS, Kingma I, de Looze MP, van Dieën JH
source.sample: 11 healthy male subjects (same cohort/ethics protocol NL57404.029.16 and identical demographics as Koopman 2019)

protocol.summary: Symmetric lifting of a 10 kg box (35 x 10 x 25 cm, w x h x d) from 10 cm above ankle height (ANKLE) or 10 cm above knee height (KNEE), box centre 35 cm (NEAR) or 60 cm (FAR) in front of the ankle joint; start and end upright without box; free (self-selected) speed and technique; 3 repetitions; WITHOUT exoskeleton condition only. Peak values over the lift. EMG: bilateral RA, EO, anterior IO, IL, LL per Kingma et al. 2010 (levels/distances not stated). Normalisation: %MVC, MVC per McGill 1991 (supine maximal efforts, as in Koopman 2019); rectified, low-pass 2.5 Hz.
how_to_simulate: Scale model to a 184 cm, 74.8 kg male

Drive the model with a symmetric 10 kg box lift from the 4 pick-up locations (box centre 35 or 60 cm anterior to ankle, 10 cm above ankle or knee height), peak lumbar flexion 31/38/48/56 deg (KN/KF/AN/AF), peak trunk angular velocity 157-232 deg/s
Compare the peak of the mean IL+LL (bilateral) activation over the lift with the measured peak %MVC

subject_model.source: Koopman 2020a Methods 2.3 (mean of 11 males; 1.84 ± 0.07 m, 74.8 ± 7.4 kg)

protocol.notes: WITHOUT means printed on Fig. 3 bars: peak lumbar flexion KN 31, KF 38, AN 48, AF 56 deg (SD digitised ~5/10/11/10); peak trunk angular velocity KN 157, KF 180, AN 216, AF 232 deg/s. Peak abdominal EMG analysed but not plotted (only ANOVA in Table 1) - not extracted. L5S1 compression is EMG-driven model output - not extracted as a measured test.
